notes: Structured data for the seven Schedules. These are reference tables used by rules 5, 11, 12 and 19-23 (see lm_pc_2011_rules.json). None of them are independently 'checkable' from a package photo without either a physical test (First/Fifth/Sixth/Seventh Schedule) or a commodity-category classification the AI layer does not perform with legal certainty (Second/Third/Fourth Schedule) -- classification is surfaced to the human inspector as a suggestion, never as an automated verdict.

firstSchedule.reason: Requires opening/weighing/measuring the physical package contents (see Rules 19-22, Sixth Schedule). Can only be used as a REFERENCE TABLE by a human inspector performing a physical check, or by a future feature that ingests declared-vs-measured quantity pairs typed in by an inspector.

secondSchedule.title: Commodities to be packed in specified (standard) quantities
secondSchedule.reason: Net quantity is OCR-readable; membership in the standard-size list below is then a deterministic lookup. fifthSchedule.title: Manner of selection of sample packages
fifthSchedule.samplingMethod: Random selection from top, bottom, centre, right, left, front and rear of stored stock; or, for in-line filling, either sampling already-filled packages at random or introducing pre-weighed marked empty containers at random into the packing line.
fifthSchedule.reason: Defines a physical sampling procedure for an on-premises inspection; not applicable to a single submitted photo.

sixthSchedule.title: Determination of the net quantity of commodities in packages
parts: Part I - Equipment: working standard weights/balances/measures, verified and functioning, to be provided to the inspecting officer.

Part II - Weight determination procedure: tare-weight determination (using empty tare packages or by opening a sample), thresholds against the maximum permissible error to decide whether more tare samples are needed, gross-minus-tare net weight calculation, and a destructive-testing alternative using marked empty containers introduced into the packing line.
Liquid content determination by volume: via specific gravity (if constant) or by pouring into a calibrated volume measure.
Verification of length: via calibrated steel tape or a calibrated longer instrument.
Verification of commodities packed by number: by actual counting, opening packages as necessary.
Checking of other declarations: examined at factory or depot level for conformity and adequacy, including the Rule 6(1)(f)/(g) declarations.
sixthSchedule.reason: A laboratory/field weighing-and-measuring procedure requiring physical equipment; explicitly PHYSICAL_TEST_REQUIRED, never inferred from a photograph.
